hero.heading: Organization architecture to complement company and product architecture
hero.lede: What has actually worked building teams from zero to one, and the org shape that follows from it.

intro.heading: A third architecture: who owns the other two
paragraphs: OneTrust has a company architecture, CPS and AEP, and a technical architecture, the seven layers in this proposal. Both need an org built for them, not assigned after the fact.

orgChart.eyebrow: Build and grow, zero to one
orgChart.heading: One structure, two functions
orgChart.description: Build: 3 direct reports, 3 dotted lines in from CPS. Small enough to move fast, tethered enough to ship into production.

directReports.note: Entity resolution, knowledge graph, policy graph

grow.label: Grow
grow.note: Existing engineering org, unchanged. Receives finished AEP capability through the facade contract, not an unfinished experiment.

releaseEngineering.heading: The gate that stops vision-to-value drift
releaseEngineering.description: Architecture without a release gate is a diagram, not a discipline. Every release checks against the contract it was designed to honor, or it doesn't ship.

gates.name: Contract conformance
gates.detail: Breaks the facade contract → build fails

gates.name: Schema versioning
gates.detail: Breaking change → new version, never a silent rewrite

unifiedPlatform.heading: One unified platform, three businesses on top
unifiedPlatform.description: No architect per business. One ultra-core team owns the identity graph, policy engine, and release gates that all three run on.

platform.label: Unified Platform
platform.note: Ultra-core: architect-builders, one ownership line, one release gate

bmad.heading: Does BMAD change how the team builds?
paragraphs: Yes, and it's not the end state. BMAD-style structure is what closed the 4-hour to 20-minute production gap at Silver Labs: a repeatable way to turn a vague ask into a spec an agent can run.

What comes after is agentic-first, closer to Kiro: workflow adapts to the task instead of the task fitting a fixed set of stages. Sequence, not a permanent pick: structure first because it ships, then agentic-first once the platform is ready.

closing.text: One design, not three: Build small on the dotted line into CPS. Grow without absorbing unfinished work. Own architecture once, gate every release against it.
